title: TLS fails on Windows with Avast HTTPS scanning: bundled mbedTLS rejects Avast's root certificate (empty AuthorityKeyIdentifier)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.2-stable (self-compiled with `precision=double` and .NET; `thirdparty/mbedtls` unmodified, mbedTLS 3.6.7).

### System information

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Avast Antivirus with HTTPS scanning enabled (default)

### Issue description

Avast intercepts TLS and re-signs server certificates with its own root "Avast Web/Mail Shield Root", which it installs into the Windows ROOT store. Godot loads that store, but the bundled mbedTLS cannot parse this root because it has an empty AuthorityKeyIdentifier extension (`30 00`). Godot logs `Error parsing X509 certificates ... -9568` (`-0x2560`) and "1 certificates skipped", and every intercepted connection then fails with `-0x2700` (certificate verify failed). Schannel, OpenSSL and browsers accept the same root.

Effect: `WebSocketPeer` (wss) and `HTTPRequest` (https) fail with a TLS handshake error on any machine with Avast HTTPS scanning. The only workarounds are an exception in the antivirus or `TLSOptions.client_unsafe()`, neither of which is reasonable to ask of players.

Upstream bug: Mbed-TLS/mbedtls#10253 (open since 2025-06, still unfixed on `development`); a PR with a fix and tests is being prepared there. Until it lands in the 3.6 LTS branch, a small patch in `thirdparty/mbedtls/patches` would fix it: in `x509_get_authority_key_id()` (`library/x509_crt.c`), right after the `*p + len != end` check:

```c
    /* All fields are OPTIONAL, so an empty SEQUENCE is valid. */
    if (*p == end) {
        return 0;
    }
```

(Edited: an earlier version suggested treating `MBEDTLS_ERR_ASN1_OUT_OF_DATA` like `UNEXPECTED_TAG`. That is too loose, since `OUT_OF_DATA` is also returned for a `[0]` tag with a missing or truncated length.)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows with Avast installed, HTTPS scanning on.
2. Request an HTTPS URL that Avast intercepts (github.com was intercepted here):

```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready():
	var request := HTTPRequest.new()
	add_child(request)
	request.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _headers, _body): print(result, " ", code))
	request.request("https://github.com")
```

3. Result is `RESULT_TLS_HANDSHAKE_ERROR`; the same request succeeds in a browser on that machine.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The script above on an empty scene is the whole project. The bug needs Avast's certificate in the Windows store, so it will not reproduce on machines without Avast.
